evidence.note:
Code review finding review-1(b) from fm/wh-passage-editor branch.

Consent UI and documentation must plainly state that allowing command
checks trusts the project's own scripts at the commit they run on.
Consent covers the command line (argv), not the scripts those commands
call, which can change through merged pull requests without turning

Drop wording that implies any change to what runs turns consent off.
Keep: changing a command line turns consent off again.

evidence.note:
Code review finding review-1 from fm/wh-passage-editor branch (commits
b24e464→923c61f). Command checks must not run in the clone's working tree
(which may have stale or unrelated code), but in a temporary git worktree
checked out at the pinned commit.

For ref: merge.commit, use the task's merge commit.
For ref: pr.head, use the pull request head.
Otherwise, use the default-branch tip (clone's defaultRef, e.g. origin/main).

Worktree path must be deterministic per run (e.g., named from task id,
check id, and commit). The worktree must be removed afterwards with
`git worktree remove --force <path>`, including when the command fails
or times out. Never use rm with globs or variables for cleanup.

evidence.note:
Code review finding review-2 from fm/wh-passage-editor branch
(TestPanel.svelte line 60).

The test panel's "Also run these commands" consent checkbox must be
tied to the exact command list the captain saw when ticking the box,
not to whatever commands are in the current draft.

Race condition: captain sees command list A, ticks the checkbox,
then edits A into B in the YAML view, and submits before the draft
refreshes. Currently, B runs on the captain's machine, though the
checkbox listed A.

Fix: send the digest of the commands listed (commandsDigest of the
draft's commands at the time of submission) with the test request.
Server's dryRun endpoint must refuse with 409 when the digest differs
from the actual text's commands, similar to the commands-consent endpoint.

Also reset runCommands whenever the listed commands change, so the
tick does not carry over to newly displayed commands.

title: Test panel command consent tied to displayed command digest

Code review finding (severity: warning): pairRounds and conversation() disagree about resolved lines without answers. When a non-answer resolve is followed by a re-raised needs-decision on the same key, pairRounds marks the round closed (line 76-80) while conversation() treats it as a new round (conversation.ts:157). This causes rounds to be skipped, answers split across multiple findings, and card display to show wrong question pairings. Example: needs-decision at t1, resolved without answer at t2, needs-decision at t3, resolved with answer at t4 results in missing t3 round, wrong t4 answer pairing, and inconsistent display between card and conversation.

Code review finding (severity: warning): When a finding id is not found in the answer text, fallback regex matches the id anywhere. Single-letter ids ('a', 'b') can match ordinary words (e.g., 'Add a guard' matches id 'a'). This causes wrong calls to be applied. Example: "Decision for key K: FIX both. Add a guard" would mark finding 'a' with call 'guard.' (verdict 'Decided' with reason 'Guard.') while 'b' correctly gets 'Fix it'.

Code review finding (severity: info): Guide documentation at line 51 lists decision filters as 'Fix it, Keep as is, Defer' but the code (decisions page and this feature) now includes a 'No change' verdict and filter. Documentation is out of date.

Commit implementing fixes for the three code review findings: makes pairRounds treat non-answer resolved lines the same as conversation() by closing the round (so later needs-decision opens a new round), drops the match-anywhere fallback in callsFor regex to require ids at call start or followed by colon/call word, and updates guide to list 'No change' filter.
